title: The Timelike Tube Theorem in Curved Spacetime
version: arXiv:2303.16380v1, 29 March 2023; pages 1-5 and 10-16, 18-19 read through a page extraction
locator: Sec. 1 (statement, timelike envelope, Holmgren analogy, history); Sec. 2 (reformulation); Sec. 4.2 (proof); Sec. 4.3 (Reeh-Schlieder)
assumptions: Globally hyperbolic real analytic spacetime; additive algebras generated by local fields; a dense set of analytic states.
conclusion: Authors' statement: the algebra of an open set equals that of its timelike envelope; the classical counterpart is Holmgren uniqueness for standard relativistic wave equations.
proof_status: Informal explanation of a proof given in their arXiv:2302.02709, which was not read.
relevance: Gives the observer statement and supports the classical thin-tube remark.
open_questions: Envelope of a half-infinite worldline in spacetimes with horizons.

title: Entanglement between the future and past in the quantum vacuum
version: arXiv:1003.0720v1, 3 March 2010, 4 pages; published Phys. Rev. Lett. 106, 110404 (2011), not compared
assumptions: Massless scalar field; calculation in two spacetime dimensions; discrete-mode approximation for the state.
conclusion: Authors' claims: massless fields in the future and past cones can be quantized as independent systems; the Minkowski vacuum is an entangled state of them; an inertial detector with a scaled energy gap responds thermally.
proof_status: Derivation by mapping to the Rindler case, read. Not re-derived.
relevance: The entanglement entry of the note.
open_questions: Their claim that the result is general for massless fields.

title: Timelike Entanglement Entropy Revisited
locator: Sec. II (timelike tube theorem and definition); Sec. IV (entanglement across time, citing Buchholz 1977 and Olson-Ralph); acknowledgments (Witten's remark on strong subadditivity)
assumptions: Additive algebras, split property, primitive causality.
conclusion: Authors' claims: timelike entanglement entropy of a worldline interval equals the entropy of its causal diamond; for even-dimensional massless free fields the future and past cones are entangled systems, which is not generally true for massive or interacting theories.
relevance: Source for the Buchholz attribution and the massless/massive contrast in the quantum case.
limits: The Buchholz result is taken on their citation.

title: Total sets in quantum field theory
relevance: Reported by a search snippet to study sets whose algebra coincides with that of a larger set, with the open past light cone as an example.
limits: Publisher page returned an access error. Nothing beyond the snippet was seen. The claim that the larger set is all of spacetime for a massive free field is unverified.
